newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli planes rocket hills south of Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes rocket hills south of Beirut.

text.p: Israeli jets rocketed Palestinian guerrilla targets in hills south of Beirut on Tuesday after earlier raids into eastern and southeastern Lebanon, Palestinian officials said.

The jets fired two rockets into the seaside Na'ameh hills where the radical Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine-General Command (PFLP-GC) has bases, a PFLP-GC official said. Na'ameh is 15 km (nine miles) south of Beirut.
"Two rockets were fired into Na'ameh hills, one exploded and the other did not," the PFLP-GC official told Reuters.

There was no immediate confirmation from independent sources of the raid which came more than an hour after Israeli jets raided a PFLP-GC base in southeastern Lebanon and rocketed a Hizbollah radio transmission station near the eastern town of Baalbek.
Security sources said the radio went off the air after the antenna was hit.

The pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war on some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied local militia holding a border zone in south Lebanon to ward off cross-border attacks on northern Israel.
